examples.ko: 고양이가 제 침대 발치에서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping at the foot of my bed.

examples.ko: 할머니의 발치에 앉아서 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I sat at my grandmother's feet and listened to her stories.

examples.ko: 강아지가 제 발치를 졸졸 따라다녀요.
examples.en: The puppy follows close at my feet.

examples.ko: 담요를 발치에 접어 두었어요.
examples.en: I folded the blanket at the foot of the bed.

examples.ko: 발치에 떨어진 열쇠를 주웠어요.
examples.en: I picked up the key that had fallen near my feet.

examples.ko: 산 발치에 작은 마을이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.

explain: 발치는 몸의 발 쪽이나 어떤 것의 맨 아래쪽을 말할 때 써요. 침대의 머리 쪽은 '머리맡', 발 쪽은 '발치'예요. 치과에서 이를 뽑는 '발치'(拔齒)는 소리만 같은 다른 말이니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: The puppy is sitting at the foot of the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 침대의 발 쪽을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for the foot end of a bed.

phrases.en: The child sits by mom's feet and plays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 발 가까이에 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being right near someone's feet.

phrases.en: We rested for a moment at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이나 언덕의 맨 아래쪽을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also mean the very bottom of a mountain or hill.

explain_en: 발치 is the foot-end of something, such as a bed. The head end of a bed is '머리맡' and the foot end is '발치'. At the dentist '발치' (拔齒, pulling a tooth) is a different word with the same sound, so tell them apart by context.

en: to seep through; to soak through

examples.ko: 이마에 땀이 배어나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Sweat started to seep out on my forehead.

examples.ko: 그 글에는 작가의 슬픔이 배어나요.
examples.en: The writer's sadness comes through in that piece.

examples.ko: 목소리에서 피곤함이 배어났어요.
examples.en: Tiredness came through in his voice.

examples.ko: 옷에 땀이 배어나서 불편해요.
examples.en: Sweat has soaked through my clothes, so I feel uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 그의 말투에서 정이 배어나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel warmth coming through in the way he speaks.

examples.ko: 손바닥에 땀이 배어나서 긴장한 게 티가 났어요.
examples.en: Sweat seeped out on my palms, so it was obvious I was nervous.

explain: 속에 있던 것이 겉으로 스며 나온다는 느낌이에요. 땀처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 쓰고, 슬픔이나 정처럼 말투나 글에서 느껴지는 감정에도 써요. 비슷한 '묻어나다'는 손이나 옷에 묻는 것에도 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: It was hot, so sweat seeped out on my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀이 천천히 겉으로 나오는 모습을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paints the picture of sweat slowly coming out.

phrases.en: Sadness seeped through his voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말투나 글에서 감정이 느껴질 때 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when emotion can be felt in someone's voice or writing.

phrases.en: Warm affection comes through in that photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배어나다와 비슷하게 감정이 겉으로 드러날 때 쓰고, 손이나 옷에 묻는 것에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 배어나다 for feelings showing through, and also used for things rubbing off onto hands or clothes.

explain_en: Liquid or feeling comes out through a surface (땀이 배어나다) It gives the feel of something inside seeping out to the surface. It is used for visible things like sweat and also for feelings such as sadness or warmth that you sense in someone's speech or writing. The similar '묻어나다' can also be used for something that rubs off onto hands or clothes.

en: naked person; person with no clothes on

examples.ko: 아이들이 벌거숭이로 개울에서 물놀이를 했어요.
examples.en: The children played in the stream with no clothes on.

examples.ko: 산불이 나서 산이 벌거숭이가 됐어요.
examples.en: After the wildfire, the mountain became bare.

examples.ko: 벌거숭이 땅에 다시 나무를 심고 있어요.
examples.en: They are planting trees again on the bare land.

examples.ko: 그 개울은 낮에 벌거숭이 아이들의 놀이터였대요.
examples.en: I heard that stream was a playground for naked kids in the daytime.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 여름마다 벌거숭이처럼 뛰어놀았어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I ran around like a little naked child every summer.

examples.ko: 나무를 다 벤 뒤 벌거숭이 산만 남았어요.
examples.en: After all the trees were cut down, only a bare mountain was left.

explain: 옷을 입지 않은 아이나 사람을 가리킬 때도 쓰지만, 요즘은 나무나 풀이 없는 '벌거숭이산'처럼 비유로도 자주 나와요. 산이 헐벗은 모습은 '민둥산'이라고도 해요. 사람에게 쓸 때는 주로 어린아이 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The mountain became bare because of the forest fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 없는 산을 비유로 말할 때 쓰는 합성어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound word for a mountain without trees.

phrases.example: 나무를 너무 많이 베어서 민둥산이 되었어요.
phrases.en: Too many trees were cut, so it became a bald mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌거숭이산과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with nearly the same meaning as 벌거숭이산.

phrases.en: A naked child runs around in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입지 않은 어린아이를 귀엽게 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to affectionately describe a small child with no clothes.

explain_en: It can refer to a child or person wearing no clothes, but it often appears figuratively too, as in '벌거숭이산' (a mountain with no trees or grass). A bare mountain can also be called '민둥산'. When used for people, it is mostly heard in stories about small children.

en: to widen and close alternately; to flare; to sniff

examples.ko: 강아지가 코를 벌름거리며 냄새를 맡아요.
examples.en: The puppy sniffs, its nose twitching.

examples.ko: 아이가 코를 벌름거리면서 빵 냄새를 맡았어요.
examples.en: The child wiggled his nose as he smelled the bread.

examples.ko: 화가 난 듯 콧구멍을 벌름거렸어요.
examples.en: He flared his nostrils as if he were angry.

examples.ko: 토끼가 코를 벌름거리는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: The way the rabbit twitches its nose is cute.

examples.ko: 그는 코를 벌름거리다가 재채기를 했어요.
examples.en: He twitched his nose and then sneezed.

examples.ko: 소가 코를 벌름거려서 가까이 가기 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The cow was flaring its nostrils, so it was scary to go near.

explain: 주로 '코를 벌름거리다'처럼 코나 콧구멍이 넓어졌다 좁아졌다 하는 모습에 써요. 냄새를 맡거나 화가 났을 때, 숨을 크게 쉴 때 자주 나와요. 가슴이 뛰는 것에는 '벌렁거리다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping with its nose flaring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌름거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 조금 더 가볍게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 벌름거리다; it sounds slightly lighter in speech.

phrases.en: The horse breathes with its nostrils flaring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '코' 대신 '콧구멍'을 넣어 넓어졌다 좁아지는 모습을 더 정확히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 콧구멍 (nostrils) instead of 코 describes the widening and narrowing more precisely.

phrases.en: The puppy's twitching nose is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 '-는'으로 바꿔서 명사 '코'를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb takes the -는 ending to modify the noun 코 (nose).

explain_en: It is mainly used in '코를 벌름거리다', for a nose or nostrils that widen and narrow repeatedly. It often appears when sniffing, being angry or breathing hard. For a pounding heart, '벌렁거리다' is more common.

en: to be convex; to be rounded; to be bulging

examples.ko: 임신해서 배가 볼록해요.
examples.en: She is pregnant, so her belly is rounded out.

examples.ko: 볼록한 유리 렌즈로 글씨를 크게 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the letters bigger through a convex glass lens.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 나니 배가 볼록했어요.
examples.en: After the meal my belly was round.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 가운데가 볼록하고 입구는 좁아요.
examples.en: This cup bulges in the middle and has a narrow mouth.

examples.ko: 볼록한 거울은 넓은 곳을 비춰 줘요.
examples.en: A convex mirror shows a wide area.

examples.ko: 호주머니가 볼록해서 뭐가 들었는지 궁금했어요.
examples.en: His pocket was bulging, so I wondered what was inside.

explain: 배, 볼, 호주머니처럼 둥글게 나온 곳에 주로 써요. '볼록한'으로 꾸미고, 가운데가 들어간 것은 '오목하다'예요. 크게 불거지면 '불룩하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The baby's round cheeks are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼록한'은 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요. 볼이 통통할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '볼록한' modifies the noun, often for plump cheeks.

phrases.example: 이 옷을 입으면 배가 볼록해 보여요.
phrases.en: In this outfit, my belly looks rounded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say it looks that way from outside.

phrases.en: This cup's bottom doesn't bulge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼록하다'의 부정형이에요. 평평하거나 들어갔다는 뜻이 될 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form; the surface may be flat or dented.

explain_en: Smaller, softer, often cute or neutral roundness. It is used for places that stick out round, such as a belly, cheek or pocket, and you modify nouns with '볼록한'. Something dented in is '오목하다', and something bulging a lot is '불룩하다'.

t90.ax: After the meal my belly was round.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 손깍지를 끼고 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: The two of them walked slowly with their fingers interlaced.

examples.ko: 손깍지 낀 채로 한참 하늘을 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up at the sky for a long time with my fingers laced together.

examples.ko: 손깍지가 풀리지 않게 꽉 잡았어요.
examples.en: I held on tightly so our interlaced fingers wouldn't come apart.

examples.ko: 그는 손깍지로 무릎을 감싸고 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat with his knees wrapped in his interlaced hands.

examples.ko: 손깍지는 이렇게 손가락 사이사이에 끼우는 거예요.
examples.en: You do a hand clasp by putting your fingers between each other like this.

examples.ko: 손깍지만 끼고 가만히 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: I just sat still with my hands clasped.

explain: '손깍지를 끼다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 연인이 손을 잡는 장면이나 머리 뒤로 손을 모으는 자세를 말할 때 자주 써요. 팔을 가슴 앞에서 엇갈리게 하는 '팔짱'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: He unclasped his hands and shook hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깍지 낀 손을 다시 푼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to undo clasped hands.

phrases.en: I lay down with my hands clasped behind my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하게 쉬는 자세를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a relaxed resting posture.
phrases.en_equiv: to clasp hands behind one's head

phrases.en: I clasped my hands together and prayed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '손깍지를 끼다'를 줄여서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened way to say 'sonkkakji-reul kkida'.

explain_en: The most natural pairing is '손깍지를 끼다' (to interlace one's fingers). It is often used for couples holding hands or for putting hands behind one's head. It is different from '팔짱', which is folding arms across the chest.

examples.ko: 아기가 쌔근쌔근 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is sleeping, breathing softly.

examples.ko: 쌔근쌔근 숨 쉬는 소리가 귀여워요.
examples.en: The sound of soft, steady breathing is so cute.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 옆에서 쌔근쌔근 잠들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling fell asleep breathing softly beside me.

examples.ko: 아이가 쌔근쌔근 자는 모습을 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the child sleeping peacefully for a long while.

examples.ko: 강아지도 쌔근쌔근 숨을 쉬며 자요.
examples.en: The puppy also sleeps breathing softly.

examples.ko: 달리기를 하고 와서 쌔근쌔근 숨을 몰아쉬었어요.
examples.en: He came back from running and was panting for breath.

explain: 주로 아기나 어린 동물이 곤히 자면서 가늘고 고르게 숨 쉬는 모양에 써요. 달리고 난 뒤 숨이 찬 모양에도 쓰지만, 잠든 모습이 훨씬 자주 떠올라요. 따뜻하고 귀여운 느낌의 말이에요.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌔근쌔근'보다 조금 더 순한 느낌으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels a bit gentler and is used often.

phrases.en: The baby sleeps breathing softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌔근쌔근'을 동사로 쓴 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 쌔근쌔근.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping soundly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊이 푹 잔다는 뜻으로 소리 흉내말 없이 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sleeping deeply, without a sound word.

explain_en: It mostly describes a baby or young animal breathing thinly and evenly in deep sleep. It can also describe panting after running, but the sleeping image comes to mind first. It has a warm, cute feel.

en: soothing touch; healing hand; comforting hand

examples.ko: 할머니의 약손 덕분에 아픈 배가 금방 나았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my grandmother's healing hands, my stomachache went away quickly.

examples.ko: 배가 아플 때마다 어머니가 약손으로 쓸어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Whenever I had a stomachache, my mother rubbed it with her soothing hand.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 엄마의 약손만 있으면 하나도 안 아팠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I didn't hurt at all as long as I had my mom's healing touch.

examples.ko: 엄마 손은 약손이라며 아이의 배를 쓰다듬었어요.
examples.en: Saying that mom's hand is a healing hand, she stroked the child's belly.

examples.ko: 친구의 따뜻한 위로가 약손처럼 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: My friend's warm comfort felt like a healing touch.

examples.ko: '엄마 손은 약손이다' 하고 말하면 신기하게 아프지 않았어요.
examples.en: When she said 'Mom's hand is a healing hand,' strangely it stopped hurting.

explain: 아픈 곳을 어루만져 낫게 해 주는 사랑이 담긴 손이라는 느낌이에요. 아이의 배를 문지르며 '엄마 손은 약손'이라고 말하는 전통적인 말이 유명해요. 사람의 따뜻한 위로를 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 엄마 손은 약손이라서 만지면 안 아파요.
phrases.en: Mom's hand is a healing hand, so it doesn't hurt when she touches it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 아이를 달래 줄 때 쓰는 전통적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A traditional phrase used to soothe a child who is hurting.
phrases.en_equiv: Mom's hand is a healing hand

phrases.en: Grandma rubbed my tummy with her healing hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 곳을 사랑으로 어루만져 주는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes lovingly rubbing a sore spot.
phrases.en_equiv: to rub with a healing hand

phrases.en: The teacher's words were like a healing touch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻한 위로가 마음을 편하게 했다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for warm comfort that eased the heart.
phrases.en_equiv: to be like a healing touch

explain_en: It carries the feeling of a loving hand that eases pain by stroking the sore spot. The traditional line '엄마 손은 약손' (Mom's hand is a healing hand), said while rubbing a child's belly, is well known. It is also used figuratively for a person's warm comfort.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 짚신을 신고 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: People in the old days walked the roads in straw shoes.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 짚신을 직접 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen straw shoes in person at a museum.

examples.ko: 짚신은 쉽게 닳아서 자주 새로 만들었대요.
examples.en: They say straw shoes wore out easily, so people made new ones often.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 어릴 때 짚신을 삼아 신으셨대요.
examples.en: They say my grandfather wove his own straw shoes as a child.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서는 짚신 모양 기념품을 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells souvenirs shaped like straw shoes.

examples.ko: 한복에 짚신을 신으니 옛날 사람이 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: Wearing straw shoes with hanbok makes me feel like a person from the old days.

explain: 짚으로 엮어 만든 옛날 신발이라서 지금은 박물관, 민속 행사, 사극에서 볼 수 있어요. 신발을 만들 때는 '삼다'를 써서 '짚신을 삼다'라고 해요. 입는 건 '신다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 걱정하지 마세요. 짚신도 짝이 있다고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Don't worry. They say even straw shoes have a pair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무리 부족해 보이는 사람도 잘 맞는 짝이 있다는 속담이에요. 결혼이나 연애 걱정을 하는 사람을 위로할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even someone who seems lacking has a good match out there. It is used to comfort someone worried about marriage or dating.
phrases.en_equiv: There's a lid for every pot.

explain_en: It is an old-style shoe woven from straw, so today you see it in museums, folk events and historical dramas. The verb for making it is '삼다', as in '짚신을 삼다'. Wearing it uses '신다'.

examples.ko: 할머니 옷에서 은은한 체취가 나요.
examples.en: Grandma's clothes carry her gentle, familiar scent.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 아버지의 체취를 맡으니 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Smelling my father's scent after a long time put my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 강아지는 체취로 주인을 알아봐요.
examples.en: Dogs recognize their owners by their scent.

examples.ko: 사람마다 체취도 다르고 좋아하는 향도 달라요.
examples.en: Everyone's body scent is different, and so are the fragrances they like.

examples.ko: 그리운 체취에 이끌려 방문을 열었어요.
examples.en: Drawn by a familiar scent I missed, I opened the door.

examples.ko: 그 방에는 이제 체취만 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Only their scent remains in that room now.

explain: 몸에서 나는 냄새를 말하는데, '땀 냄새'나 '몸 냄새'와 달리 그 사람만의 냄새를 부드럽게 표현해서 그리움이나 분위기를 담을 때가 많아요. 글이나 감성적인 말에서 잘 나오고, '작가의 체취'처럼 개성이 느껴질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I can smell my mother's scent in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 사람만의 냄새가 은은하게 느껴질 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for a person's own faint scent being noticeable.

phrases.example: 이불에 아직 할머니의 체취가 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: My grandmother's scent still lingers on the blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 떠난 뒤에도 냄새가 남아 그리움이 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the scent remains after the person is gone, evoking longing.

phrases.en: I can feel the author's personal touch in this writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새가 아니라 개성이나 분위기가 느껴진다는 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use meaning personality or atmosphere is felt, not literal smell.

explain_en: It refers to a person's body smell, but unlike '땀 냄새' or '몸 냄새' it softly describes that person's own scent, often carrying longing or atmosphere. It fits writing and emotional speech, and can also mean a personal touch, as in '작가의 체취'.

en: to be hollow-eyed; to be sunken (eyes)

examples.ko: 며칠 잠을 못 자서 눈이 퀭해요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days, so my eyes look sunken.

examples.ko: 요즘 얼굴이 퀭해 보여서 걱정했어요.
examples.en: You've looked hollow-faced lately, so I was worried.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 다들 눈이 퀭하더라고요.
examples.en: During exams, everyone's eyes look hollow.

examples.ko: 눈이 퀭한 친구를 보고 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I saw my friend with sunken eyes and bought him a meal.

examples.ko: 밤샘 근무 후에 거울을 보니 눈이 퀭했어요.
examples.en: After the all-night shift, my eyes looked sunken in the mirror.

examples.ko: 오래 아파서 볼이 퀭하게 들어갔어요.
examples.en: After being sick for a long time, his cheeks became hollow.

explain: 주로 '눈이 퀭하다'처럼 피곤하거나 아파서 눈이 쑥 들어가고 기운이 없어 보일 때 써요. 볼이나 얼굴에도 쓸 수 있어요. 그냥 눈이 깊은 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니라, 지치고 야윈 모습을 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: After working overtime for days, my eyes have become sunken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 피곤해서 눈이 쑥 들어간 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for eyes that look sunken from fatigue.

phrases.example: 퀭한 눈으로 병원 복도에 앉아 있었어요.
phrases.en: He sat in the hospital hallway with hollow eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun.

phrases.en: My cheeks have become hollow since I got sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈뿐 아니라 볼이 야위어 쑥 들어간 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for cheeks that look thin and sunken, not just eyes.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '눈이 퀭하다' when someone's eyes look sunken and lifeless from tiredness or illness. You can also use it for cheeks or a face. It is not for people who simply have deep-set eyes; it carries a worried tone about someone looking worn out and thin.

examples.ko: 아버지는 오 년 동안 암과 투병하셨어요.
examples.en: My father fought cancer for five years.

examples.ko: 투병하는 동안 가족의 응원이 큰 힘이 됐어요.
examples.en: My family's support was a great strength while I was fighting my illness.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 건강이 나빠져 한동안 투병했어요.
examples.en: That singer's health got worse and she struggled with illness for a while.

examples.ko: 투병하면서도 웃음을 잃지 않는 친구가 대단해요.
examples.en: My friend, who keeps smiling even while fighting illness, is amazing.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 투병해 온 선배가 드디어 퇴원했어요.
examples.en: My senior, who had been fighting illness for a long time, was finally discharged.

examples.ko: 투병하느라 학교를 쉬었지만 올해 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I took a break from school to fight my illness, but I came back this year.

explain: '병을 앓다'가 병에 걸린 상태라면, '투병하다'는 병에 오래 맞서 싸우는 과정에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 짧은 감기보다 암처럼 긴 병에 쓰고, '투병 생활', '암 투병'이라는 말로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: My grandmother lived through a long illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병과 싸우며 지내는 시간을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for the time spent fighting an illness.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 암 투병 끝에 무대로 돌아왔어요.
phrases.en: The singer returned to the stage after fighting cancer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름 뒤에 '투병'을 붙여 어떤 병과 싸우는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after a disease name to say which illness one is fighting.

phrases.example: 친구 어머니가 투병 중이라 병원에 자주 가요.
phrases.en: My friend's mother is fighting an illness, so she often goes to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 병과 싸우는 중이라는 현재 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone is currently in the middle of fighting an illness.

explain_en: While '병을 앓다' describes being sick, '투병하다' focuses on the long process of fighting an illness. So it fits long illnesses such as cancer rather than a short cold, and it often appears as '투병 생활' or '암 투병'.

en: to be pale; to be wan; to be pasty

examples.ko: 어디 아파요? 얼굴이 해쓱해 보여요.
examples.en: Are you sick? You look pale.

examples.ko: 며칠 앓았더니 얼굴이 해쓱해졌어요.
examples.en: After being sick for days, my face became pale.

examples.ko: 해쓱한 얼굴로 병원에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: She came out of the hospital with a pale face.

examples.ko: 밤을 새워서 안색이 해쓱하네요.
examples.en: You stayed up all night, so your complexion looks pale.

examples.ko: 놀란 아이의 얼굴이 해쓱하게 질렸어요.
examples.en: The startled child's face went pale.

examples.ko: 그는 해쓱하다 못해 창백할 지경이었어요.
examples.en: He was so pale that he looked almost ashen.

explain: 몸이 안 좋거나 놀라서 얼굴에 핏기가 없을 때 써요. 거의 얼굴이나 안색에만 쓰고, '핼쑥하다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 일상 대화에서는 '창백하다'나 '안색이 안 좋다'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: He came out of the hospital with a pale face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 핏기 없는 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form placed before the noun, describing a face with no color.

phrases.en: I was so shocked that my face turned pale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해쓱하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 해쓱하다 and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 어제 만났을 때 친구가 많이 해쓱했어요.
phrases.en: My friend looked very pale when I met him yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로, 그때 본 안색을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form, used to describe how someone looked at that time.

explain_en: It describes a face drained of color from illness or shock, and is almost only used for the face or complexion. It is used much like '핼쑥하다'. In daily talk '창백하다' or '안색이 안 좋다' is more common.

t90.ax: Are you sick? You look pale.

examples.ko: 할머니가 쑥을 넣어서 개떡을 쪄 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother steamed gaetteok with mugwort for me.

examples.ko: 간식으로 먹던 개떡이 갑자기 생각나요.
examples.en: I suddenly remember the gaetteok we used to eat as a snack.

examples.ko: 개떡은 모양이 투박하지만 맛은 구수해요.
examples.en: Gaetteok looks plain, but it tastes nutty and good.

examples.ko: 갓 쪄 낸 개떡 냄새가 온 집에 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The smell of freshly steamed gaetteok spread through the house.

examples.ko: 개떡하고 식혜를 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate gaetteok together with sikhye.

examples.ko: 이 개떡에는 쌀가루와 쑥이 들어갔어요.
examples.en: This gaetteok has rice flour and mugwort in it.

explain: 곡식 가루를 반죽해서 납작하게 쪄 만든 소박한 떡이에요. '쑥개떡'처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 부르기도 해요. '개떡 같다'는 '형편없다'는 뜻의 거친 말이라서 조심해서 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 개떡같이 말해도 찰떡같이 알아들어요.
phrases.en: My team leader gets what I mean even when I say it badly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 서툴거나 모호해도 상대가 뜻을 정확히 이해할 때 써요. 칭찬하는 농담 같은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone understands the exact meaning even though what was said is clumsy or vague. It has a playful, complimentary tone.
phrases.en_equiv: to understand what you mean even when you say it badly

explain_en: It is a humble rice cake made by kneading grain flour and steaming it flat. People sometimes put the ingredient first, as in '쑥개떡' (mugwort gaetteok). '개떡 같다' is a rough way to say something is terrible, so be careful with it.

examples.ko: 무쇠솥에 밥을 하면 누룽지가 맛있어요.
examples.en: If you cook rice in a cast iron pot, the scorched rice is delicious.

examples.ko: 시골집에는 아직 무쇠솥이 있어요.
examples.en: The house in the countryside still has a cast iron pot.

examples.ko: 무쇠솥은 처음 쓸 때 길을 들여야 해요.
examples.en: You need to season a cast iron pot when you first use it.

examples.ko: 무쇠솥은 무거워서 옮기기 힘들어요.
examples.en: A cast iron pot is heavy, so it's hard to move.

examples.ko: 이 무쇠솥 하나로 찌개도 끓이고 밥도 해요.
examples.en: I make both stew and rice with this one cast iron pot.

examples.ko: 선물로 받은 무쇠솥을 잘 닦아서 보관했어요.
examples.en: I cleaned the cast iron pot I got as a gift and put it away.

explain: 재료인 '무쇠'로 만든 솥을 부르는 말이에요. 비슷한 '가마솥'은 크고 부뚜막에 거는 솥을 먼저 떠올리게 해요. 새로 산 무쇠솥은 기름으로 '길들이다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to a countryside restaurant to eat rice cooked in a cast iron pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무쇠솥'에 '밥'을 붙인 말로, 무쇠솥에 지은 밥을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '밥' attached to '무쇠솥', meaning rice cooked in a cast iron pot.

phrases.en: I rubbed oil on the new cast iron pot to season it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 산 무쇠솥을 기름으로 처리해서 쓰기 좋게 만드는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treating a newly bought cast iron pot with oil so it is ready to use.
phrases.en_equiv: to season a cast iron pot

phrases.example: 국을 무쇠솥에 끓이면 더 깊은 맛이 나요.
phrases.en: Soup boiled in a cast iron pot has a deeper taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 무쇠솥을 요리 도구로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '에' marks the cast iron pot as the cooking vessel.
phrases.en_equiv: to boil in a cast iron pot

explain_en: It names a pot made of cast iron ('무쇠'). The similar word '가마솥' makes people picture a large pot set over a traditional hearth first. For a new cast iron pot, you say you '길들이다' (season) it with oil.
